points.why: It says blame isn't a model output, that a verdict would fail politically, and that parties will pick self-serving baselines, but it frames the dispute as mainly an empirical question rather than a disagreement about what the problem is.

It proposes drawing the stocks and flows with stakeholders so each group recognizes its flow, but never asks for explicit agreement on the boundary or a record of who was consulted versus only informed.
It names the commons structure (shared, unpriced stock, each user rational to keep pumping) and prescribes a shared, visible, metered and enforced rule instead of blame.
It recommends building the model anyway, uses the hydrographs to test the dry-years story, and insists on building it with the stakeholders.

pitfalls.why: It explicitly refuses to present a finished verdict and says to build the model with stakeholders without naming a culprit.
